subtopics.title: Why Do We Need Version Control?

steps.say: Without version control, copies pile up: final, final_v2, FINAL_really…
As the project grows, nobody knows which copy is latest, who changed what, or how to go back.
Version control is the better solution: one project, with its history saved as snapshots.
Git records how your project develops over time — it is more than a place to store files.

g.text: Every change keeps an author, a date and a message

subtopics.title: Why Do We Need a Remote Repository?

steps.say: Your project and its commits live only on your laptop.
Teammates, or your other machine, cannot reach it.
A remote repository stores the Git repository outside your local environment.
Developers exchange commits and collaborate on one shared codebase.

s.text: Publish changes · retrieve updates · work together

modules.title: Git in a Real DevOps Workflow

subtopics.title: Connect Git to the DevOps Lifecycle

steps.say: Your work starts on your machine: develop, commit, push.
GitHub hosts the repository and coordinates review.

gh.text: GitHub hosts the repo · coordinates collaboration

steps.say: Then automation takes over: test, build and deploy — without repeating every step by hand.
Every change travels the same reliable path.
Make your change, then review what Git sees.
Leave out unrelated changes, generated files and sensitive configuration.
Commit the relevant files. This records the change in the repository’s history.
Your commit exists only on your computer.
Push the branch and set its upstream.
Your teammates can now access the branch. Open a pull request to propose the change.
The team inspects the changes, discusses the implementation, and checks that required checks passed.
A GitHub Actions workflow can run when a pull request is opened.
It installs dependencies…
…executes automated tests…
…and builds the frontend and the backend.
CI keeps checking that the software stays in a working state.
After the required checks pass, the next stage is preparing or releasing the application.
Continuous Delivery keeps the application releasable. Production may still need an approval.
Continuous Deployment releases to production automatically after the checks pass.
The right approach depends on test coverage, operational needs and tolerance for risk.

both.text: Both make releases more consistent and less manual

steps.say: Workflows are YAML files stored in the repository, commonly under .github/workflows/.
A workflow runs in response to events: a pull request, a push to a branch, or a manual trigger.
For example, this workflow runs tests whenever a pull request is opened.
Tests pass — and nobody had to run them by hand.
